_comment: Template for scripts/memory-sync.sh. Copy to ~/.claude/memory-sync.json, fill in your shared org-tier repo, and add ~/.claude/memory-sync.json + ~/.claude/.memory-sync/ to your sync exclusions (never distribute this filled copy). See CLAUDE.md, 'Sharing instincts/memory across a team (org tier)'.

gate._comment: Shared by scripts/memory-sync.sh (promote path) and scripts/artifact-gate.sh (shipped-artifact sweep). ipAllowlist is a regex of IPv4 prefixes that are NOT reported, e.g. an internal VPN net. denyNames is the list of tenant and project names that must never appear in a shipped artifact or in promoted memory; it is matched case-insensitively as a literal substring, and the names themselves are never echoed into gate output. Keep this file out of every repository -- putting the names into a tracked file would leak exactly what the check protects. A CI job that cannot read this file can pass the same list via the CCPR_GATE_DENY_NAMES environment variable (newline- or comma-separated) from its secret store.

conformance._comment: Read by scripts/conformance-run.sh (docs/adr/ADR-0010-conformance-runs-against-consumers.md). consumers is a list of real projects this operator maintains, addressed by LOCAL FILESYSTEM PATH ONLY -- nothing is ever fetched over a network. Each consumer's id is what reports show; the path never appears in a report unless --show-paths is given. optional (default false) means a missing path is reported as not-covered instead of failing the run -- useful for a consumer that lives on a machine this config is also used from, but is not always checked out. pins (Wave 3, not read yet by this wave's script) will be concrete, dated, per-consumer expectations -- each needs a why. Keep this file out of every repository, same reasoning as gate.denyNames above: a consumer's path is frequently a home directory.
